usage: Very common everyday word for going to work; it is much more natural in spoken Cantonese than a formal expression.
Often used with time words like 返工前, 返工後, and 啱啱返工 to talk about work routines and schedules.
Can be used as a verb on its own: 返工 means to go to the workplace/start work for the day.
In casual speech, it also appears in questions about work life, shifts, and commuting, especially when talking about weekdays.

examples.jyutping: ngo5 ting1jat6 jiu3 zou2 di1 faan1 gung1.
examples.meaning: I have to go to work earlier tomorrow.
What time do you go to work?

examples.jyutping: keoi5 mui5jat6 daap3 baa1si2 faan1 gung1.
examples.meaning: He/she takes the bus to work every day.

examples.sentence: 病都冇請假返工，真係辛苦。
examples.jyutping: beng6 dou1 mou5 ceng2 gaa3 faan1 gung1, zan1 hai6 san1fu2.
examples.meaning: Going to work without taking sick leave is really tough.
